import importlib.util
for name in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','PIL','reportlab','pypdfium2']:
    spec=importlib.util.find_spec(name)
    print(name, spec.origin if spec else None)
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
print('META',r.metadata)
parts=[]
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages):
    t=p.extract_text()
    parts.append(f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i+1} =====\\n\\n'+t)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(parts))
print(''.join(parts[:3]))
PY"

strengths: AugSub offers a useful, simple training contribution: shared weights connect a conventionally trained branch with a more strongly regularized branch supervised by detached predictions. The method adds no inference overhead, and its fixed 50% masking ratio transfers across substantially different training recipes.

The main ImageNet evidence is convincing. Table 3 reports gains across all four ViT sizes: 0.6–0.7 percentage points at 400 epochs and 0.3–0.5 points at 800 epochs. Tables 4–5 extend the evaluation to pretrained transformers, ResNets, and Swin. Repeated-run results in Tables A.1–A.2 strengthen the central findings.

The manuscript meaningfully addresses additional training cost. In Table 6, AugMask ViT-B achieves 84.1% with 25 GPU-days versus 83.7% with 26 GPU-days for longer baseline training. Favorable comparisons also appear for MAE fine-tuning, supporting practical value under comparable computational budgets.

Evaluation extends well beyond ImageNet validation accuracy. Table 7 shows improvements across every reported robustness metric, including ImageNet-A gains from 51.9% to 58.3% for ViT-H. Segmentation, detection, and transfer experiments provide additional evidence that the learned representations remain useful downstream.

The core algorithm is easy to understand and implement. Appendix B documents substantial training and hardware details, selected experiments include three-run statistics, and the manuscript provides a code link. These are meaningful reproducibility strengths.
weaknesses: The originality claim is stronger than the comparison establishes. The method combines familiar self-distillation and stochastic regularization through asymmetric branches. Section 2 acknowledges the closely related Co-sub framework, but provides no direct experimental comparison. Consequently, the distinct advantage over existing sub-model training methods remains uncertain.

The ablations do not isolate the proposed relaxed supervision. Table 1 compares AugSub against training only the regularized model, while AugSub also retains supervised learning on the conventional branch. A matched two-branch control using ground-truth supervision for both branches is absent. The evidence therefore establishes that the complete method works more clearly than it establishes why detached soft targets are responsible.

The explanation of automatic prioritization overstates what the objective guarantees. The auxiliary logit gradient depends on the difference between branch predictions, rather than ground-truth correctness; confident incorrect predictions can still provide strong supervision. Furthermore, detaching teacher outputs does not isolate shared parameters from sub-model gradients. Figure 3 supports an observed gradient trend, but does not establish the claimed exclusive regularization of successfully learned examples or guaranteed protection of main-model convergence.

Several smaller improvements have limited statistical support. The 0.1-point BEiT v2 and Swin-T gains and the 0.2–0.3 AP detection/instance-segmentation gains lack variability estimates. Some transfer improvements in Table A.3 are also smaller than the reported standard deviations. These results are encouraging, but describing all improvements as significant is insufficiently supported.

The practical claims need clearer boundaries. Adding AugMask during fine-tuning reduces ViT-B CIFAR-100 accuracy from 91.9% to 89.6% in Table 10, and Section 4.2 states that CLIP's best checkpoint accuracy is unchanged. Training also costs approximately 1.5 times as much for token-dropping ViTs and twice as much for ResNet/Swin. These limitations qualify its value as a broadly applicable plug-in, although they do not outweigh the supported main results.
